items.q: By the end of this decade, the carmaker ______ more than half of its plants to fully automated lines.
items.vi: Đến cuối thập kỷ này, hãng xe sẽ chuyển đổi xong hơn một nửa số nhà máy của mình sang dây chuyền hoàn toàn tự động.
items.explanation: By the end of this decade is a future deadline, and an action finished before a future point takes the future perfect: will have converted. ✗ has converted — present perfect reports what is already done now, not by a future date; ✗ will convert — simple future says the action happens, not that it is complete by the deadline; ✗ is converting — present continuous describes something in progress now.

items.q: In an effort to curb obesity, the government has decided to ______ a levy on sugary drinks from next April.
items.vi: Nhằm kiềm chế béo phì, chính phủ đã quyết định áp một khoản thuế lên đồ uống có đường từ tháng Tư năm sau.
items.explanation: Governments impose a tax, levy, ban or fine — the verb that collocates with a levy. ✗ inflict — cause pain, damage or defeat on someone; ✗ impart — pass on knowledge, news or a flavour; ✗ install — fit equipment or software in place.

items.q: If the shares keep sliding, you may be wiser to ______ now than to wait years for a recovery that may never come.
items.vi: Nếu cổ phiếu tiếp tục trượt giá, có lẽ bạn nên cắt lỗ ngay bây giờ thay vì chờ đợi nhiều năm cho một sự phục hồi có thể chẳng bao giờ đến.
items.explanation: The clue shares keep sliding … than wait years for a recovery points to giving up before losing more: cut your losses = stop a failing venture early. ✗ cut corners — do a job cheaply or carelessly; ✗ cut a long story short — skip to the summary; ✗ cut your teeth — gain your first experience of something.

items.q: Regulators must ______ a balance between protecting consumers and leaving room for innovation in the fintech sector.
items.vi: Các cơ quan quản lý phải tìm được sự cân bằng giữa việc bảo vệ người tiêu dùng và tạo dư địa cho đổi mới trong lĩnh vực công nghệ tài chính.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is strike a balance (also strike a deal, strike a chord); the clue is a balance between. ✗ hit — hit a target or a wall, never a balance; ✗ beat — beat an opponent or a record, not a balance; ✗ knock — knock on a door or knock something over, no link with balance.

items.q: Once the outcry over the product recall had ______, the company quietly relaunched the toy under a new name.
items.vi: Khi làn sóng phẫn nộ về vụ thu hồi sản phẩm đã lắng xuống, công ty lặng lẽ tung lại món đồ chơi dưới một cái tên mới.
items.explanation: Anger, noise or a controversy dies down = gradually becomes less intense, which fits an outcry that later lets the company relaunch. ✗ died out — disappear completely, used of species or customs; ✗ died away — fade to silence, used of a sound or wind; ✗ died off — die one after another, used of living things.

items.q: The economist ______ forecasts the ministry relied on has admitted that her model ignored energy prices entirely.
items.vi: Nhà kinh tế có các dự báo mà bộ đã dựa vào thừa nhận rằng mô hình của bà hoàn toàn bỏ qua giá năng lượng.
items.explanation: The forecasts belong to the economist, so the possessive relative whose goes before the noun forecasts (= the economist's forecasts). ✗ whom — object pronoun for a person, cannot own a noun; ✗ which — refers to things and would leave forecasts without an owner; ✗ that — subject/object relative, shows no possession.

items.q: Several hospitals have ______ a strict no-visitor policy during the flu season to protect vulnerable patients.
items.vi: Nhiều bệnh viện đã áp dụng chính sách cấm thăm bệnh nghiêm ngặt trong mùa cúm để bảo vệ những bệnh nhân dễ tổn thương.
items.explanation: To adopt a policy is to start using it, and the clue a strict no-visitor policy during the flu season is something new the hospitals took up. ✗ adapted — change something to suit new conditions; ✗ adjusted — alter slightly, fine-tune; ✗ accommodated — provide room for or meet someone's needs.

items.q: ______ had the central bank cut interest rates than the currency began to slide against the dollar.
items.vi: Ngân hàng trung ương vừa mới cắt giảm lãi suất thì đồng nội tệ đã bắt đầu trượt giá so với đô la.
items.explanation: The second clause opens with than, which pairs only with No sooner + inverted past perfect (No sooner had … than …). ✗ Hardly — needs when, not than; ✗ Scarcely — also needs when; ✗ Not until — must introduce a time clause first (Not until X did Y) and never takes than.

items.q: Before signing up for any 'free' trial, shoppers should always ______, since a monthly fee usually kicks in after thirty days.
items.vi: Trước khi đăng ký bất kỳ gói dùng thử 'miễn phí' nào, người mua nên luôn đọc kỹ các điều khoản in nhỏ, vì thường sau ba mươi ngày sẽ bắt đầu bị tính phí hằng tháng.
items.explanation: The clue a monthly fee usually kicks in after thirty days is a hidden condition, so read the fine print = check the small, easily missed terms of a contract. ✗ read between the lines — work out a meaning that is not stated; ✗ read the riot act — scold someone severely; ✗ read them like a book — understand someone's thoughts easily.

items.q: Tracking down the so-called miracle cure turned out to be a wild ______ chase that ______ the family thousands of dollars.
items.vi: Việc săn lùng cái gọi là thần dược hóa ra là một cuộc truy tìm vô vọng khiến gia đình tốn hàng nghìn đô la.
items.explanation: The idiom for a hopeless search is a wild goose chase, and a thing that makes you lose money costs you that amount (the chase cost the family thousands). ✗ duck / charged — no 'wild duck chase'; charge needs a seller as subject; ✗ fox / paid — not the idiom; the family, not the chase, would pay; ✗ hare / spent — not the idiom; spend needs a person as subject.

items.q: The patient ______ the medication as prescribed — his blood tests show no trace of it whatsoever.
items.vi: Bệnh nhân không thể nào đã uống thuốc theo đơn — xét nghiệm máu của anh ta không cho thấy chút dấu vết nào của thuốc.
items.explanation: The clue no trace of it whatsoever makes it impossible that he took the drug; a confident negative deduction about the past is can't have + past participle. ✗ shouldn't have taken — criticises a past action that did happen; ✗ needn't have taken — he took it but it was unnecessary; ✗ must have taken — positive deduction, the opposite of the evidence.

items.q: Researchers ______ a large-scale trial across twelve countries to test whether the vaccine protects adults over seventy.
items.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu đã tiến hành một thử nghiệm quy mô lớn tại mười hai quốc gia để kiểm tra liệu vắc-xin có bảo vệ người trên bảy mươi tuổi hay không.
items.explanation: You conduct a trial, survey, experiment or investigation — the verb that collocates with a large-scale trial. ✗ directed — direct a film, traffic or a company; ✗ governed — govern a country, or rules that govern behaviour; ✗ steered — steer a vehicle or a conversation.

items.q: Sales of organic food have doubled in five years, ______ the number of certified organic farms has barely changed.
items.vi: Doanh số thực phẩm hữu cơ đã tăng gấp đôi trong năm năm, trong khi số trang trại được chứng nhận hữu cơ hầu như không thay đổi.
items.explanation: Sales doubled while farms barely changed — two contrasting full clauses, joined by the conjunction whereas. ✗ despite — a preposition, must be followed by a noun or -ing, not a clause with a verb; ✗ consequently — signals a result, but the second fact is not caused by the first; ✗ otherwise — means 'if not', which makes no sense here.

items.q: Antibiotic resistance ______ a far greater threat to public health than most consumers realise.
items.vi: Tình trạng kháng kháng sinh đặt ra mối đe dọa với sức khỏe cộng đồng lớn hơn nhiều so với những gì hầu hết người tiêu dùng nhận thấy.
items.explanation: The collocation is pose a threat (also pose a risk / a problem / a question); the clue is a … threat to. ✗ puts — you put someone at risk, but never put a threat; ✗ places — place a bet or an order, not a threat; ✗ sets — set a target or a record, not a threat.

items.q: The auditors recommended that every branch ______ its accounts to head office by the end of each quarter.
items.vi: Các kiểm toán viên khuyến nghị rằng mỗi chi nhánh phải nộp sổ sách kế toán về trụ sở chính trước cuối mỗi quý.
items.explanation: After recommended that (also suggest / insist / demand that) the verb takes the subjunctive base form: every branch submit. ✗ submits — the indicative -s form is not used in the subjunctive clause; ✗ submitted — past tense, but the recommendation is about what should happen; ✗ will submit — will is not used after recommend that; the base form already means 'should submit'.

items.q: Rather than admit that the failed product launch was his own doing, the manager ______ in front of the whole board.
options: threw his assistant under the bus
items.answer: threw his assistant under the bus
items.vi: Thay vì thừa nhận vụ ra mắt sản phẩm thất bại là do chính mình, người quản lý đã đổ hết trách nhiệm lên trợ lý của mình trước toàn thể hội đồng quản trị.
items.explanation: The clue rather than admit … was his own doing means he shifted the blame: throw someone under the bus = sacrifice a colleague to protect yourself. ✗ threw down the gauntlet — issue a challenge; ✗ threw in the towel — give up, admit defeat; ✗ threw caution to the wind — act recklessly, take a risk.

items.q: Many retailers now regret ______ so heavily in city-centre stores just before online shopping took off.
items.vi: Nhiều nhà bán lẻ giờ đây hối tiếc vì đã đầu tư quá mạnh vào các cửa hàng ở trung tâm thành phố ngay trước khi mua sắm trực tuyến bùng nổ.
items.explanation: Regret + -ing = feel sorry about something already done, and the clue just before online shopping took off places the investing in the past: regret investing. ✗ to invest — regret to + infinitive only introduces bad news you are about to give (we regret to inform you); ✗ invest — regret never takes a bare infinitive; ✗ to have invested — not a standard pattern after regret; the -ing form already refers to the past.

items.q: Parliament ______ a law last month requiring supermarkets to print the unit price on every shelf label.
items.vi: Tháng trước, Quốc hội đã ban hành một đạo luật yêu cầu các siêu thị in đơn giá trên mọi nhãn kệ hàng.
items.explanation: A legislature enacts (passes) a law — the clue is Parliament … a law. ✗ enforced — make people obey a law that already exists, the job of police or regulators; ✗ entailed — involve something as a necessary part; ✗ enabled — make something possible.

items.q: The trade talks ______ for almost three years, costing exporters billions in lost orders.
items.vi: Các cuộc đàm phán thương mại kéo dài lê thê gần ba năm, khiến các nhà xuất khẩu mất hàng tỷ đô la đơn hàng.
items.explanation: Something tedious that lasts far longer than it should drags on; the clue for almost three years and the missing object show the intransitive verb is needed. ✗ dragged out — transitive: someone drags the talks out, so it needs an object; ✗ dragged in — involve someone in a matter unnecessarily; ✗ dragged along — bring someone somewhere unwillingly.

items.q: ______ with last year's figures, the hospital's average waiting time has fallen by almost a third.
items.vi: So với số liệu năm ngoái, thời gian chờ trung bình của bệnh viện đã giảm gần một phần ba.
items.explanation: The subject the hospital's average waiting time is the thing being compared, so the passive past participle Compared with is needed (= when it is compared with). ✗ Comparing — active -ing would make the waiting time do the comparing; ✗ To compare — infinitive of purpose ('in order to compare'), which the sentence does not express; ✗ Having compared — active perfect participle, again needs a person as subject.

items.q: Trying to work out why the price of eggs had doubled, the reporter ______ of feed costs, tariffs and bird flu.
items.vi: Cố tìm hiểu vì sao giá trứng tăng gấp đôi, phóng viên đã sa vào mê cung của chi phí thức ăn chăn nuôi, thuế quan và cúm gia cầm.
items.explanation: The clue trying to work out why … of feed costs, tariffs and bird flu shows the reporter got lost in an ever more complicated topic: go down a rabbit hole — the only option that takes of + the topic. ✗ went off the deep end — lose your temper suddenly; ✗ went round in circles — make no progress; ✗ went up the wall — become extremely annoyed.

items.q: The rural clinic ______ its doors last spring if the local council hadn't stepped in with an emergency grant.
items.vi: Phòng khám nông thôn hẳn đã phải đóng cửa vào mùa xuân năm ngoái nếu hội đồng địa phương không kịp thời hỗ trợ một khoản trợ cấp khẩn cấp.
items.explanation: The if-clause hadn't stepped in plus the past time last spring make an unreal past condition — third conditional, so the result takes would have closed. ✗ would close — second conditional, for an unreal present or future; ✗ had closed — past perfect belongs in the if-clause, not the result clause; ✗ will have closed — future perfect, but the situation is past and did not happen.

items.q: Only trained nurses are permitted to ______ the vaccine, which has to be injected slowly into the upper arm.
items.vi: Chỉ những y tá đã qua đào tạo mới được phép tiêm vắc-xin này, loại vắc-xin phải được tiêm chậm vào bắp tay.
items.explanation: To administer a drug or vaccine is to give it to the patient, which fits nurses … injected slowly into the upper arm. ✗ prescribe — a doctor writes the order for a medicine; ✗ apply — put a cream or dressing on the skin; ✗ undergo — what the patient does: undergo surgery or a treatment.

items.q: Mask factories ran around the clock, yet they still could not ______ the demand during the first weeks of the outbreak.
items.vi: Các nhà máy khẩu trang chạy suốt ngày đêm nhưng vẫn không thể đáp ứng nhu cầu trong những tuần đầu của đợt bùng phát dịch.
items.explanation: Demand, a deadline, a target or a need is met = satisfied, and the clue could not … the demand points to this collocation. ✗ reach — reach a level, a target or an agreement, not demand; ✗ hit — hit a target or a record, not demand; ✗ catch — catch a bus, a cold or a ball, not demand.

items.q: Lawyers were asked to ______ up a contract that would ______ either side from walking away before the merger was complete.
items.vi: Các luật sư được yêu cầu soạn thảo một hợp đồng ngăn không cho bên nào rút lui trước khi vụ sáp nhập hoàn tất.
items.explanation: A contract or plan is drawn up = written out in detail, and prevent someone from doing something is the verb that takes from. ✗ set / avoid — set up a company, not a contract; avoid takes an object or -ing, never 'someone from'; ✗ make / refuse — make up a story, not a contract; refuse to do, never 'someone from'; ✗ put / deny — put up a building or a price, not a contract; deny something, never 'someone from'.
